name: Political philosophy
summary: Political philosophy is the philosophical study of the foundations of politics: the state, legitimacy, authority, justice and liberty. Scholarship treats it as a field in which rival schools argue, not as a body of doctrine with positions of its own.
scope: The field as the defining scholarship (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entries on ancient political philosophy and political legitimacy) describes it: a genre of inquiry begun by the Greeks and carried on through many schools. Positions of any school (liberalism, socialism, Platonism and so on) are excluded as borrowing; only what the field as such holds counts, which is almost nothing.
